title.suggested: Tom Allen Discharged on Assault Charge

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat reported that Tom Allen was tried in the Court of Criminal Correction for assault to kill Joseph P. Moore in a Fourth of July fight at his saloon, and was discharged on the evidence.

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The St. Louis Democrat: St. Louis, Saturday, August 2, 1873'; masthead 'Daily Democrat'. Pre-1875 merger.

facts.fact: Joseph P. Moore said Allen beat and kicked him after Moore fought a waiter in Allen's Washington Avenue saloon, laying him up twelve days in the City Hospital
places: Tom Allen's saloon, Washington Avenue, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen was tried in the Court of Criminal Correction on a charge of assault to kill and was discharged on the evidence
places: Court of Criminal Correction, St. Louis

notes: Captain Burgess and a dozen policemen came to testify to Allen's good character but were not needed.
